content:
alex: Quick recap from the authz visibility workshop — main ask from PMs: make it obvious in the console which requests are being billed to org vs project keys. right now users get confused when service accounts route to a fallback project.
maria: +1. We should also surface when a request fell back to a compatible model/variant due to quota. That was causing noise in support. :thinking_face:
sam: Agree — two separate signals: (1) attribution (org/project/service-account) and (2) routing decision (primary model/variant vs fallback). Need to decide data surface in telemetry and how the console shows it.
jordan: For telemetry schema proposal: add `key_origin` (values: org|project|service_account|proxy), `effective_project_id`, `routing_reason` (e.g., capacity_fallback, latency_policy, model_unavailable). These are small strings we can tag in traces.
nisha: We also need a sampling plan. If we attach full `request_headers` to every span, customers will complain about PII. Proposal: sample 1% of requests with full headers, 100% with just `key_origin` and `model_variant`.
oncall-bot: NOTE: deploy scheduled for canary tomorrow at 03:00 UTC. Expect 5% rollout.
alex: UX idea: Console top-line card shows: "Attribution: 82% Project, 15% Org, 3% Service account" and a link "Show fallback events" toggling a table of `routing_reason`. Keep it collapsed by default.
maria: That sounds reasonable. For billing we must guarantee attribution is deterministically computed server-side (no client inference). Otherwise customers will get mismatched invoices.
sam: Implementation note: attribution should be computed before any token exchange or impersonation proxy happens. So we need to pipe original credential metadata to the attribution pipeline. Edge case: delegated tokens — we should attach an `orig_credential` identifier.
jordan: About quotas: if a request uses a project key but routes to a dedicated pool billed to org commit, do we attribute quota burn to project or org? Finance wants billing tied to commit owner (org), but console owner wants project-level visibility.
nisha: Proposed compromise: show both. Expose `billing_owner` (org_id) and `logical_owner` (project_id). Default aggregation in console uses `logical_owner` but invoices and quota deductions use `billing_owner`.
alex: That dual-owner surface will help support triage. Add a tooltip: "billing_owner used for billing and reserved capacity; logical_owner used for usage attribution in dashboards."
sam: Rollout plan: opt-in flag `authz.attribution.dual_owner=true` enabled for canary orgs. We'll collect telemetry for 48h and validate invoice parity on a sample account.
maria: On telemetry retention — keep attribution tags for 90 days in high-cardinality index, aggregated metrics for 365 days. Need SRE sign-off for storage cost.
oncall-bot: ACTION: deploy-bot scheduled canary at 2026-03-24T03:00:00Z.
deploy-bot: Canary started: 5% traffic -> eng-platform-canary. Logs: `canary_ok=0` for ~2 requests out of 12k (expected).
jordan: Implementation checklist: 1) add `key_origin` and `billing_owner` to tracer payload, 2) ensure attribution set before proxy exchange, 3) UI card + collapsed fallback table, 4) sampling + privacy filter, 5) canary flag.
nisha: Quick security note: do NOT surface full service-account email in UI by default. Use hashed id and allow expansion to full email for customers with role. Audit log on access.
alex: 👍 let's sync on PRs tomorrow. If no objections I'll merge the console mockups and telemetry schema into `auth-specs` repo.
maria: No objections from me.
sam: Fine with me.
jordan: LGTM.
nisha: LGTM but please add the audit log requirement to the spec.
alex: Thanks everyone — will open the PR and tag the oncall for the canary window.
